rationale: The strongest answer to whether weekly reporting reduces emergency visits in this centre would come from allocating new patients in the two clinics that have not started. Trials elsewhere (claims c1 and c5) suggest a benefit, and a pragmatic trial would test it in routine conditions with the centre's own staffing.
alternatives: Explanatory sequential mixed methods evaluation of the rollout in the two running clinics
Before-after comparison of emergency visits in the breast and colorectal clinics
whyNotMoreComplex: A cluster design across all four clinics would need more clinics than the centre has.

decision.statement: Randomise patients starting chemotherapy in the lung and head-and-neck clinics from January 2027 to weekly reporting or usual telephone triage for their first three cycles, with emergency visits and admissions as the primary outcome.
decision.question: Does weekly electronic symptom reporting reduce emergency visits and admissions in this centre's routine care?

criteria.text: Weekly reporting reduced emergency visits in randomised trials.
The centre has already committed to offering weekly reporting to every patient, leaving no equipoise for withholding it.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval for allocating new patients to delayed weekly reporting
Rollout committee agreement to withhold weekly reporting from control patients for three cycles

alternatives: Mixed methods evaluation of the rollout in the breast and colorectal clinics
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 and c5; both gates are unknown.

summary: Pragmatic trial proposed; both gates are unknown.
